central_model: An iterative, hybrid taxonomy-development method: define a purpose-driven meta-characteristic and explicit ending conditions; alternate empirical-to-conceptual and conceptual-to-empirical passes; revise dimensions and characteristics until objective and subjective utility criteria are met.

architecture_principles.principle: Anchor every classification field in one meta-characteristic derived from the taxonomy’s intended users and use.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Keeps report-, study-, workflow-, link-, contrast-, validation-, and evidence-level fields coherent while preventing a grab-bag schema.

architecture_principles.principle: Model each unit with dimensions whose characteristics are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive; each object receives exactly one characteristic per dimension.
architecture_principles.source_locator: “Problem statement for taxonomy development,” formal definition of taxonomy, p. 340
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Makes coding comparable and auditable, while allowing several orthogonal dimensions rather than forcing unlike entities into one hierarchy.

architecture_principles.principle: Use both empirical-to-conceptual and conceptual-to-empirical development, selecting the route per iteration based on available cases and domain knowledge.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Empirical records expose real analytic variation; conceptual passes protect coverage of important causal concepts not yet frequent in the corpus.

architecture_principles.principle: Iterate by adding, splitting, merging, or removing dimensions and characteristics, then retest the taxonomy.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Supports an evolving review without pretending its first data model is final.

architecture_principles.principle: Separate objective closure checks from subjective usefulness checks.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Objective checks catch redundancy and incomplete category support; subjective checks protect concision, explanatory value, and practical usability.

architecture_principles.principle: Preserve explanatory dimensions rather than exhaustive descriptive detail.
architecture_principles.why_it_manages_complexity: Focuses the model on distinctions that explain causal workflows and claims, rather than duplicating every detail of a paper.

unit_and_boundary_rules: Treat the source report as a container, not as the sole analytic object. A report may describe multiple studies, workflows, contrasts, links, validations, and supporting evidence items.
Define a study as the bounded empirical investigation or dataset/application context being analyzed; a report can contain one or more studies.

Define a causal workflow as an ordered analytic procedure within a study, including its causal-estimation strategy and assumptions. Do not merge distinct workflows merely because they occur in the same report.
Define a causal link as one asserted exposure/intervention-to-outcome relationship within a workflow; retain direction and endpoints as separate fields.
Define a contrast as the specific comparison or estimand used to support a causal link; retain it separately from the link because one link may be assessed through multiple contrasts.
Define validation as an assessment activity applied to a workflow, link, or contrast, not as an attribute that replaces the analytic result.
Define source evidence as the exact report-local support for a coded assertion, with a locator; evidence may support multiple objects and an object may require multiple evidence items.

For each entity type, make characteristics mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive within a stated dimension; use explicit “not reported/unclear” handling only when it is a deliberate characteristic rather than an implicit omission.

Do not force all entity types into a single flat taxonomy. Use linked taxonomies or dimensions for their different roles, then connect them through explicit relations. This follows the source’s allowance for multiple taxonomies and possible later merging.
provenance_and_evidence_rules: Every coded dimension or relation should be traceable to a source-evidence record containing a precise locator (page, section, table, figure, quotation, or named method).
Keep evidence separate from interpretation: record what the report states, then record the normalized coding or causal interpretation it supports.
Maintain report-to-study and study-to-workflow links so a claim can be navigated back through its analytic context to the exact supporting passage.
Record whether a dimension was supported empirically by observed report content, conceptually inferred from the review’s meta-characteristic, or both; this mirrors the source’s hybrid method.
Audit gaps explicitly: an unsupported characteristic, duplicated dimension, or unclassifiable object should trigger revision or a documented uncertainty state rather than silent normalization.

Use objective review checks adapted from Table 2: no duplicated dimensions/characteristics/combined cells; no unsupported active category; no unexamined in-scope object class; and no unreviewed change after splitting or merging an entity.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.proposed_component: A review-level meta-characteristic: “how a causal multi-omics aging claim is produced, contrasted, checked, and evidenced.”
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: Meta-characteristic is selected from purpose, intended users, and expected use (pp. 343–344).
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Use it to admit only fields that help explain causal claim production, rather than cataloguing all biological or technical metadata.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.proposed_component: A linked entity graph: Report → Study → Causal workflow → Causal link → Contrast, with Validation and Source evidence attached as independently addressable nodes.
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: The source defines taxonomies as multidimensional classifications and notes that multiple taxonomies may be developed and later merged (pp. 340, 344, 355).
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Preserves one-to-many relationships and prevents report-level metadata from being incorrectly inherited by every study or causal claim.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.proposed_component: Two development passes for the coding framework: derive candidate dimensions from observed papers, then challenge them against a conceptual causal-analysis model.
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: First capture methods actually used in aging multi-omics; then test whether the schema distinguishes assumptions, estimands, mediation/colocalization-style links, and validation modes adequately.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.proposed_component: A change-controlled codebook with split/merge history and repeated termination checks.
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: Table 2; iteration discussion of adding, eliminating, combining, splitting, and retesting dimensions (pp. 344–346).
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Allows taxonomy evolution while retaining reproducibility of earlier extraction decisions.

adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.proposed_component: A utility review using concise, robust, comprehensive, extendible, and explanatory criteria.
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.source_basis: “Problem statement for taxonomy development” and Table 3 (pp. 341–345).
adaptations_for_causal_multiomics_review.use_in_review: Evaluate whether the schema is small enough for reliable screening, rich enough to differentiate workflows, covers the corpus, accommodates new methods, and explains rather than merely lists papers.

cautions: The source offers a methodology for taxonomy development, not a validated ontology for causal inference or multi-omics; domain-specific causal definitions must be supplied elsewhere.
The source explicitly states that the method does not identify a uniquely best taxonomy and that researcher judgment remains necessary (“Discussion,” pp. 353–355).

Mutual exclusivity applies within a chosen dimension. If a causal feature genuinely has several simultaneous values, represent it through separate dimensions or linked records rather than forcing a false single category.
Conciseness and robustness can conflict; Table 3 treats their resolution as a subjective, argued judgment rather than an automatic threshold.
Use of a taxonomy over time is the source’s ultimate practical test of usefulness; initial closure conditions are necessary guidance, not proof of sufficiency (pp. 341–342, 346–347).
